record.paper_title: Current Unsolved Problems in Planetary Nebulae Research
record.original_question: What physical process first creates the asymmetries that later develop into bipolar, multipolar, or point-symmetric planetary nebula morphologies, and at what evolutionary stage do those asymmetries first appear: during the asymptotic giant branch wind, during the proto-planetary-nebula phase, or only after the fast post-AGB wind turns on?

evidence.quote: What is the origin of such asymmetries and when did they first develop?

Imaging with the HST showed that they already possess bipolar and, in some cases, multipolar shapes, which was interpreted as indicating that much of the shaping happened early in the proto-planetary nebulae phase or even in the late-AGB phase [60–63].

artifact.status_search_result: The shaping of asymmetric (bipolar, multipolar, point-symmetric) planetary nebulae remains an active and unresolved question in stellar astrophysics. The leading paradigm increasingly favors binary/companion interactions (common envelope, jets, wind Roche-lobe overflow) imprinting asymmetries during the late-AGB or proto-PN phase, supported by ALMA and HST imaging showing structure already in pre-PN sources, but no single mechanism is established as universally responsible, and the precise onset epoch is still debated. Recent reviews (e.g., Jones & Boffin; De Marco; Decin et al.) describe the problem as open.

status_evidence.title: Planetary nebulae shaped by common envelope evolution
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews evidence that binary interaction, particularly common-envelope evolution, is responsible for shaping many bipolar and point-symmetric PNe.
status_evidence.claim: Mechanism remains debated; binary shaping is favored but not proven universal.

status_evidence.title: (Sub)stellar companions shape the winds of evolved stars (Decin et al., Science 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: ALMA observations show that companions structure AGB winds into spirals, arcs, and bipolar geometries already during the AGB phase.
status_evidence.claim: Asymmetries can arise during the AGB wind through binary interaction, supporting onset prior to the fast post-AGB wind.
